text: Identified the relevant article as Federal Rules of Evidence ARTICLE VI. WITNESSES, because it is the only federal-rules article on Cornell LII whose titles contain “witnesses” throughout (Rule 601, 605, 606, 607, 608, 611, 612, 613, 614, 615, etc.). Rule 601 is the first rule in that article. Cornell’s current Rule 601 text uses “unless these rules provide otherwise,” while the 2011 Committee Note says the rule was restyled for style/terminology only. The pre-restyling submitted text quoted in the notes was “Every person is competent to be a witness except as otherwise provided in these rules,” so the deleted word was “except.”

Verified the selection criteria from Cornell LII: the Federal Rules page lists the sections in order, and the fifth section is ARTICLE V. PRIVILEGES. On that same page, ARTICLE VI. WITNESSES is the next section and is the article with the “witnesses” label in the most rule titles (Rule 605, 606, 607, 608, 611, 612, 613, 614, 615, plus the article heading itself). Rule 601 is the first rule in ARTICLE VI. The Rule 601 page shows the current text “unless these rules provide otherwise” and the 2011 notes quote the prior text “except as otherwise provided in these rules,” so the deleted word remains “except.” Sources: https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/fre ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/fre/article_VI ; https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/fre/rule_601
